sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Johnston County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Johnston County land are recorded at the Register of Deeds office on the first floor of the county courthouse in Smithfield, at 207 E. Johnston Street, Suite 209. The courthouse sits on Courthouse Square at 2nd and Market Street, and the main line for land records is 919-989-5160.

The office lists general hours of Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding county holidays. The real estate counter takes walk-ins without an appointment until 4:45 p.m. on weekdays. Vital records are a separate counter with its own number, 919-989-5161, so a seller who needs a death certificate to support an inherited sale should call that line rather than the land records line.

Recording matters because North Carolina gives priority by time of registration in the county where the land lies. A deed that has not reached the register is not protected against a later buyer or a lien creditor, so a seller selling a Johnston County house wants the deed recorded the same day the buyer funds.

sections.h2: What does the Johnston County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
A standard deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each page after that, while a deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 for pages 1 to 35. The office posted this schedule with an update date of August 30, 2024.

Johnston County Register of Deeds recording fees as printed on the county fee schedule page

Deed or other instrument (not a deed of trust, satisfaction, UCC or plat)$26.00 for the first 15 pages, $4.00 for each additional page

The same page says mailed documents that need a refund are not refunded when the amount is $1.00 or less. Larger refunds are mailed as a check from the county finance office.

sections.h2: How much is the excise tax on a Johnston County deed?
sections.html:
The county fee schedule prints the excise stamp as $2.00 per $1,000, which it also writes as $1.00 per $500 of consideration. State law sets that rate and puts the duty on the seller, so the transferor pays the register before the deed is recorded.

Half of the stamp money stays in the county general fund and the other half goes to the state Department of Revenue. The excise tax is a separate line from the page-based recording fee, and the title company normally shows both on the seller's side of the settlement statement.

Ask the office or the closing attorney what dollar amount the stamp will be on your price before closing day. Do not rely on a rough guess, since the rate applies to each $500 or fraction of it.

sections.h2: Can a Johnston County deed be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The register's office says it was one of the first in North Carolina to record every document type electronically and one of the first in the country to e-record plat maps, and it now e-records most of the documents it receives.

The county names five submitters it accepts for e-recording:

  • CSC eRecording
  • EPN
  • Indecomm
  • NTC
  • Simplifile

The office describes the benefit as turnaround in seconds, since a recorded document goes back to the submitter for review almost at once. A title company or closing attorney usually holds an account with one of these services, so a seller rarely deals with the portal directly. If you are closing without a lawyer, ask whoever handles your closing which service they use and when the file can be sent.

The county also runs an online document search. It lets a visitor look up a grantor or grantee name, a reception number, a date range or a subdivision, and it has a find-related feature for documents that share a legal description.

sections.h2: What can make a Johnston County deed cost more to record?
sections.html:
Three things add to the base charge: extra pages, extra instruments and a document that fails the state formatting standards. Each shows up on the county schedule as its own line.

  • Pages. Each page after the 15th on a deed adds $4.00.
  • Multiple instruments. Two or more instruments with different legal consequences in one document add $10.00 for each extra one.
  • Nonstandard format. A document that does not meet the recording standards in G.S. 161-14(b) carries a $25.00 charge on top of the recording fee.

Payoff paperwork is the cheap part. Satisfactions of a deed of trust, trustee satisfactions and affidavits of satisfaction carry no charge, so clearing an old loan costs nothing at the register. A seller whose lender has not yet released the lien should have the lender send the satisfaction for recording after payoff.

sections.h2: What should a seller know before the deed goes to the register?
sections.html:
Make sure the deed is signed, notarized and complete before it leaves the closing table, because the register records instruments and does not draft or fix them.

A short pre-recording checklist keeps a Johnston County closing from stalling:

  • Confirm the grantor names match the way title is currently held.
  • Include the parcel description from the prior deed.
  • Have the excise stamp amount ready for the transferor to pay.
  • Order any lender satisfaction so the old deed of trust is cleared.
  • Ask the Johnston County tax office whether any current bill is unpaid, since the property tax lien attaches to a parcel as of the January 1 listing date.

The register's office also offers a free property fraud alert service, with sign-up through the county site. Owners who rent out or leave a Johnston County house vacant during a sale may want it, since property fraud cases are on the rise according to the office.

sections.h2: What is Johnston County like for people selling a house?
sections.html:
Johnston County is a fast-growing county east of Raleigh, with 256,448 residents estimated for July 1, 2025 and a 2020 census count of 215,999. That is up 18.7 percent from the April 2020 base, and the county shows 99,408 housing units.

The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures put the median value of an owner-occupied home at $305,600, with 76.1 percent of homes owner-occupied. Median household income is $83,384, and the mean trip to work takes 32.2 minutes. Median gross rent is $1,146, so a landlord selling a rental in Johnston County often compares a sale price against steady rent.

Building activity is heavy: the county shows 3,002 building permits for 2025. For a seller, that means new construction competes with older homes, and buyers often ask for repairs or credits on a resale. Land area is 792.02 square miles, which makes Johnston a large county with both town lots and rural acreage.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited or has liens in Johnston County?
sections.html:
Start by getting the right documents recorded. Estate and probate filings go through the clerk of superior court, while the register records the deeds that follow. A small estate affidavit under North Carolina law can be used when the personal property, less liens, does not exceed $20,000, and it is filed with the clerk in the county where the decedent lived.

For liens, the register keeps the index but does not remove anything. A mortgage or deed of trust disappears from the record only when a satisfaction is recorded. Tax liens follow a different path: they attach to the parcel on the listing date, and enforcement is a foreclosure filed in the county where the land lies.

If a Johnston County house has liens, back taxes, tenants or repair problems, a direct cash sale can close without a listing, showings or repair work. The deed still goes to the same register's office and carries the same recording fee and excise stamp as any other sale.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Johnston County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call 919-989-5160 for land records and 919-989-5161 for vital records and marriage licenses. The office is on the first floor of the courthouse at 207 E. Johnston Street, Suite 209, Smithfield.

faqs.q: What is the cost to record a standard deed in Johnston County?
faqs.a: The county schedule prints $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each added page. A deed of trust or mortgage is $64.00 for pages 1 to 35. The excise stamp is paid separately at $2.00 per $1,000 of consideration.

faqs.q: Does Johnston County charge to record a satisfaction of a deed of trust?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists no charge for a satisfaction of a security instrument, a trustee's satisfaction, a notice of satisfaction, a certificate of satisfaction or an affidavit of satisfaction.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Johnston County?
faqs.a: Yes, through an accepted submitter. The county lists CSC eRecording, EPN, Indecomm, NTC and Simplifile, and your title company or closing attorney normally sends the file on your behalf.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Johnston County?
faqs.a: The seller, who is the transferor under state law. The tax is paid to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, at $1.00 for each $500 of consideration or fraction of it.
